headline: He put lead in gas. Kids paid in IQ points.

portrait.alt: Studio portrait of Thomas Midgley Jr. in round glasses, suit and polka dot tie
portrait.credit: Thomas Midgley Jr. Blank and Stoller, New York. Science History Institute. No known copyright.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Stop the knock
slides.text: Early car engines knocked, wasting power and wearing out parts. **Thomas Midgley set out to stop the knock.**
slides.alt: A busy Los Angeles intersection in 1922, with streetcars, early automobiles and a Union Gasoline station
slides.credit: North Broadway and Sunset Boulevard, Los Angeles, 1922. Automobile Club of Southern California. Public domain.

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: A pinch of lead
slides.text: In 1921 Midgley found that **a little lead in gasoline stopped the knock.** It went on sale as Ethyl, hailed as a triumph of chemistry.
slides.alt: A rusted red Atlantic gasoline pump with a yellow and blue Ethyl anti-knock compound emblem
slides.credit: Atlantic Ethyl pump, Leola, Pennsylvania. John Margolies, 1982. Library of Congress. Public domain.

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Lead in every city
slides.statLabel: IQ points lost by Americans alive in 2015, one study estimates
slides.text: For decades the lead came out of tailpipes, settled into dust and soil, and **got into children, whose brains it harms.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: The lead, yes
slides.text: Lead poisoning had been known for centuries. In 1924 workers making the additive began to die, and **the deaths made the papers.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: A century to undo
slides.text: The US finished banning leaded gas for cars in 1996. **The last country stopped selling it for cars in 2021.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Home fridges that would not poison or burn (Freon)
costs: 824 million IQ points lost by Americans alive in 2015, one study estimates
At least 15 workers killed making the lead additive
A hole in the ozone layer, still healing
slides.text: It gave engines that stopped knocking and more powerful cars and planes. **It cost 824 million IQ points, one study estimates.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: The problem moves
slides.text: The fix worked where it was aimed, inside the engine. **The harm landed in the air, the dust and children.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: Whether a fix works and who pays for it are separate questions. **Ask both before it ships.**
